Add the hard Precedence(blocker_moved, has_door_key), Precedence(has_door_key, door_open), and Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up). Keep the hard Existence(target_picked_up) as the last-step goal; together with the chain it already forces blocker_moved, has_door_key, and door_open, so no Existence clauses for those earlier steps.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: The task is a listed sequence (move the ball, then take the key, open the door with it, and pick up the box), and the clauses match the required pattern exactly: a hard Existence(target_picked_up) as the last event plus hard Precedence(blocker_moved, has_door_key), Precedence(has_door_key, door_open), and Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) between each consecutive pair. The chain with the hard Existence of the last step forces blocker_moved, has_door_key, and door_open, so no Existence clauses for the earlier steps are needed and none were added; all four events appear in 'Every way to finish includes' and trace to the task sentence. Priorities are all hard, which matches the wording (no preference cues).
